govdocs-archive_org-fer-latin-american-l: The south-of-the-border devil-knights sheaf — many hands — strings tales of devil-fellowships down south. The file fits the crank god-lore shelf. The theme draws tall talk. No one has proved the charges. Its sayings want proof. Read it with both eyes open.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AssassinationsR: This item — Assassinations: De Gaulle, CIA — is a National Security Internet Archive file on assassination plots. The file’s full context is unclear. De Gaulle survived many attempts. Researchers value such files. The item is a fragment of the intelligence archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIACubans_CIA_C: Myra MacPherson’s Associated Press piece — The Last Casualty of the Bay of Pigs — covers the failed invasion’s human cost. The 1961 invasion was a fiasco. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FensterwaldBern: Joseph Berger’s review of ‘Coincidence or Conspiracy’ is a book review. The book tackled the JFK debate. Reviews shaped the public mind. The review is measured. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Mexican-America: Peter Nabokov’s Tijerina Trial Stuns Officials is a Washington Post piece. Tijerina led the Chicano land-rights fight. The verdict shocked the establishment. The trial was historic. The file belongs to the legal archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-NewOrleansExcha: Chris Shearouse’s Change in Exchange: Dilemma in an Alley is a New Orleans piece. The alley held the city’s secrets. Alleyways tell stories. The piece is evocative. The file belongs to the cultural archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
air-service-boys-in-the-big-battle-or-si: Charles Amory Beach sends his young American aviators into the great battles of the Western Front in this World War I adventure. Daring flights, dogfights with German aces, and a mission to silence the enemy's big guns keep the heroes aloft and in peril. Written while the war still raged, it thrilled boys with the newest, most romantic branch of service.
a-treatise-on-the-six-nation-indians: J. B. Mackenzie's study tells of the Six Nations, the great Iroquois league of Mohawks, Oneidas, Onondagas, Cayugas, Senecas, and Tuscaroras. He writes of their customs, their councils, and how this strong union of tribes held together long before white settlers came. A useful early record of one of North America's great native alliances.
the-loss-of-the-s-s-titanic-its-story-an: Lawrence Beesley, a second-class passenger who survived the Titanic's sinking, wrote this clear-eyed account within months of the disaster. He describes the collision, the lifeboats, and the rescue with calm precision — and draws lessons about arrogance and unpreparedness. One of the most important firsthand records of the night the great ship went down.
missionary-work-among-the-ojebway-indian: Edward Francis Wilson recounts his missionary labors among the Ojibway of the Great Lakes — their language, customs, and conversion, recorded with sympathy and care. His detailed account preserves much about nineteenth-century Indigenous life. An important and humane record. His affection for the Ojibway people shines through every chapter.
graded-lessons-in-english-an-elementary-: Reed and Kellogg's graded lessons taught generations of American schoolchildren to diagram sentences and master English grammar. One hundred practical lessons built solid foundations, sentence by sentence. The classic American grammar that shaped how the nation learned to write well.
discipline-and-other-sermons: Charles Kingsley preaches on discipline — of body, mind, and soul — in these manly, stirring sermons. His muscular Christianity speaks plainly to duty and self-rule. Vigorous Victorian faith at its best. On work, on purity, on courage in daily life, he speaks straight to the conscience of his hearers.
early-plays-catiline-the-warrior-s-barro: Henrik Ibsen's early plays — Catiline, The Warrior's Barrow, and Olaf Liljekrans — show the young dramatist finding his voice. Romantic verse dramas before the great realistic plays, they reveal the roots of his genius. Essential for Ibsen students. The future master of the modern stage is already visible in these youthful works.
a-shepherd-s-life-impressions-of-the-sou: W. H. Hudson's Shepherd's Life preserves old Caleb Bawcombe and the vanishing world of the Wiltshire downs — a shepherd's year in loving detail. His record of rural England is now an elegy and a classic. Nature writing at its most humane.
keith-of-the-border-a-tale-of-the-plains: Randall Parrish's Keith of the Border is a tale of the plains — a scout's adventures through Indian wars and frontier perils. His hero's courage and honor never waver in the face of danger. Love and loyalty lighten the trail. A stirring Western romance in the classic manner.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-leri: This entry treats Lérins, the island abbey off Cannes. Honoratus founded it in the fifth century. Jean Besse sings its island praise. Saints have prayed there for sixteen hundred years. Vincent's Commonitory was written on its sunny shore. Two saints named Honoratus made it holy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-sain: This piece covers St. Albans, the English abbey of the first martyr. Alban's blood hallowed the Hertfordshire hill. Gilbert Huddleston gives its long history. A premier abbey of England. Matthew Paris chronicled England's kings within its walls. Its shrine drew pilgrims from every shire.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abecedarians: This 1913 reference article on the Abecedarians — the sect that scorned all book learning. John Joseph A'Becket tells their strange story. They burned books and shunned schools. Fanaticism's war on the alphabet. Luther himself argued against their book-burning zeal. Their hatred of letters died with the sect itself.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-janss: This 1913 reference article on Abraham Janssens — the Flemish painter of grand baroque scenes. George Williamson surveys his canvases. Antwerp's churches still show his work. A solid master of the Counter-Reformation. His Day and Night hang in the Vienna gallery.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acclamation-i: A 1913 entry on acclamation in papal elections — choosing a pope by sudden unanimous shout. William Fanning notes its rare use. The Spirit moves the cardinals as one. Rome's most dramatic elections. Gregory VII was hailed by the Roman crowd. Such moments were rare and momentous.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acts-of-roman: This 1913 reference article on the acts of the Roman Congregations — decrees of the Vatican's high courts. Hector Papi explains their force and form. Cardinals judged the Church's causes. Rome's tribunals, and their written word. Their Latin filled the canonists' manuals. Every diocese felt their rulings.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-advocates-of-: This 1913 reference piece on the advocates of the Roman Congregations — the canon lawyers who plead at Rome. William Fanning describes their college. They argue causes before the cardinals. The bar of the Vatican's courts. Learned pleaders in red-tape robes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aeons: This 1913 reference piece on the aeons — the shadowy emanations of Gnostic myth. John Bertram Peterson untangles their ranks. Valentinians counted thirty in all. Heresy built heavens of fancy. A guide through Gnostic mazes. Irenaeus mocked their fanciful family tree. Their names still puzzle the curious.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agents-of-rom: A 1913 entry on the agents of the Roman Congregations — the business men who transacted causes at Rome. William Fanning explains their office. Bishops hired them to plead and pay. The Vatican's antechambers knew them well. Church business, professionally done. Their fees filled the manuals of style.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexian-nuns: A 1913 entry on the Alexian Nuns — the sisters who nurse the sick. The entry traces their charitable rule. Their hospitals serve the suffering. The order's mercy knows no bounds. Handmaids of the sick poor. Their wards comfort the dying. Their veil is black, their work white.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexians: This 1913 reference article on the Alexians — the Cellite brothers of the sickbed. John Joseph A'Becket gives their history. They nursed plague victims fearlessly. Their houses spread through Germany. Charity's humble religious family. Their rule is St. Augustine's own. Their motherhouse stands in Aachen.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-algonquins: A 1913 entry on the Algonquins — the great Indian family of the northeast woods. Thomas Campbell tells their mission story. The black robes lived and died among them. Their language family spans a continent. A noble race, sorely tried. Their missions dot the Great Lakes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-horns: A 1913 entry on altar horns — the raised corners of the old altars. Augustin Schulte traces them to Scripture. The Jewish altar bore such horns. Refugees clung to them for mercy. An ancient form, long kept. Their gilding caught the candlelight.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-lantern: This 1913 reference article on altar lanterns — the lights of procession. Augustin Schulte describes their carrying. Their flames guard the Host's progress. Corpus Christi glows with their train. The Eucharist's moving guard. Their glass shields the flame from wind. Their poles bear the guilds' badges.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-linens: This 1913 reference piece on altar linens — corporals, purificators, and palls. Augustin Schulte details each one's care. Their washing is a reverent rite. The sacristy keeps them folded white. The altar's fine linen. Their starch keeps the folds crisp. Their bleaching is the laundry's pride.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amalricians: A 1913 entry on the Amalricians — the pantheist followers of Amalric of Bena. John Joseph A'Becket tells their fall. Paris burned their leaders in 1210. Their God-in-all things shocked the age. Heresy of the early university. Their ashes scattered in the Paris wind.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ambrose-berna: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Ambrose O'Higgins — the Irish governor of Chile. Thomas Meehan tells his remarkable rise. From Sligo cabin to viceroy's palace. His son Bernardo freed the nation. Ireland's gift to South America. His statue stands in Santiago's square.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ambrosians: This 1913 reference article on the Ambrosians — the Milanese religious family. Jean Besse notes their history. Their rule honored St. Ambrose. The entry preserves their modest fame. A local flower of the Lombard Church. Their houses dotted the Lombard plain. Their habit was brown and white.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-american-indi: A 1913 entry on the American Indians — the tribes and their missions. James Mooney, the great ethnologist, wrote it. His learning fills the long article. The missions' story runs through it. The continent's first peoples, fully treated. His Bureau reports are classics.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amiens: This 1913 reference piece on Amiens — the French diocese of the great cathedral. Georges Goyau gives its glory. Its Gothic nave is France's largest. The Baptist's head rests in its shrine. A see of Picardy's pride. Its weeping Virgin draws the pilgrims.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ammonian-sect: A 1913 entry on the Ammonian Sections — the Gospel divisions of Ammonius. Florentine Bechtel explains their use. Eusebius built his canons on them. The margins of old Bibles show them. The Gospels' first reference system. Their numbers edge the ancient pages.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-order: This 1913 reference piece on the Ancient Order of Hibernians — the Irish-American brotherhood. James McFaul describes its work. Its lodges aided the immigrant poor. Faith and fatherland were its motto. Erin's sons in America. Its halls span the fifty states.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ansegisus-arc: A 1913 entry on Ansegisus — the Archbishop of Sens. Michael Ott notes his Carolingian part. He crowned the West Frankish kings. The primacy of Gaul was his. A prelate of Charlemagne's heirs. His canons ruled the Frankish church. His see claimed the Gallic primacy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antediluvians: This 1913 reference article on the antediluvians — the patriarchs before the Flood. Christian Van den Biesen treats their long lives. Methuselah's years puzzle the critics. The Bible counts their generations. The world's first age. Their giants stalk the Genesis page. Their story fills the Genesis chapters.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostle-spoon: This 1913 reference piece on apostle spoons — the baptismal gifts of old England. Caryl Coleman describes their quaint use. Each spoon bore an apostle's face. The godparents gave them at the font. The nursery silver of Tudor times. Their handles end in apostle figures.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolic-can: A 1913 entry on the Apostolic Canons — the ancient church discipline. Thomas Shahan weighs their venerable text. Eighty-five rules guide the clergy. The East holds them in honor. The old law of the Church. Their text survives in Greek and Latin.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolic-con: A 1913 entry on the Apostolic Constitutions — the great ancient manual. John Bertram Peterson unfolds its eight books. Its liturgy is the oldest complete. The scholars mine its text. The encyclopedia of the early Church. Its prayers are the Church's oldest.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aquarians: This 1913 reference piece on the Aquarians — the sect of water instead of wine. Benedict Guldner notes their abstinent error. The Church condemned the watered chalice. The Eucharist needs the vine's fruit. A heresy of the second century. Their chalice held water alone.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-araucanians: This 1913 reference piece on the Araucanians — the Mapuche of Chile. Adolph Bandelier describes their proud tribes. They never bowed to the Inca or Spain. Their wars fill the colonial annals. The unconquered people of the south. Their toquis led the long resistance.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-assideans: A 1913 entry on the Assideans — the Hasideans of the Maccabean age. Anthony Maas tells their pious stand. They died for the law's sake. The faithful remnant of Israel. The saints of the persecution. Their example nerved the Maccabees. Their blood sealed the covenant's law.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-basilians: A 1913 entry on the Basilians — the orders of St. Basil's rule. John Plomer surveys their widespread houses. The East and West both claim his name. The schools and missions know their work. The monks of the great Cappadocian. Their habit is the Eastern black.
